problem:
Given that 

$$
\begin{aligned}g(x) & ={\begin{aligned}3x, & x\ne 4 \\ 13, & x=4,\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

which of the following statements are true?

- ${lim}_{x\to {4}^{+}}g(x)={lim}_{x\to {4}^{-}}g(x)$
- ${lim}_{x\to 4}g(x)=g(4)$
- $g(x)$ has a removable discontinuity at $x=4$
worked_solution:
Let's check our continuity conditions:

- $g(4)=13$ exists$\,\,✓$

- The left and right-sided limits are

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \,{4}^{-}}g(x) & ={lim}_{x\to \,{4}^{-}}3x=12, \\ {lim}_{x\to \,{4}^{+}}g(x) & ={lim}_{x\to \,{4}^{+}}3x=12.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the left and right-sided limits are equal, we conclude that statement I is true and

$$
{lim}_{x\to 4}g(x)=12.\,\,✓
$$

- The value of the limit is ${lim}_{x\to 4}g(x)=12,$ while the value of the function is $g(4)=13.$ So, statement II is false and

$$
{lim}_{x\to 4}g(x)\ne g(4)\,\,\times 
$$

Since the third condition failed, the function has a removable discontinuity at $x=4,$ and statement III is true.

In conclusion, only statements I and III are true.
